advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Decide whether _cascade_parent_first should mirror claim_compute's benign-race re-check (re-resolve the parent after a failed parent transition; if it is no longer in the eligible status, proceed with the child) or document why the divergence is intentional.
evidence: src/rebar/_commands/transition.py:464 `except CommandError as exc:` with no post-failure re-read — any parent failure aborts the child
claim.py:215 `if _resolve_open_parent(tracker, ticket_id) is None:` then `pass  # parent progressed concurrently; proceed to claim the child` — the benign-race path _cascade_parent_first lacks
claim.py:204-214 comment documents the TOCTOU: 'the cascade DECISION above read the parent as open WITHOUT the write lock' and that a peer-progressed parent is BENIGN
The reopen edge is now user-facing (rebar reopen), so the divergence is newly reachable via a documented command, not only the internal transition path
advisory.finding: _cascade_parent_first aborts the child on ANY parent CommandError, unlike claim_compute's cascade which re-checks the parent status and treats a concurrently-progressed parent as benign. On the newly-added closed->open reopen edge this means a peer that concurrently reopens the parent (closed->open) between the unlocked _resolve_parent_in_status decision-read and the locked parent transition causes the child reopen to fail with a spurious ConcurrencyError/exit 10, even though the invariant it protects (parent no longer still-closed) is already satisfied.
scenarios: Two agents reopen an epic's closed children concurrently: agent A's reopen of the shared closed parent lands first; agent B's parent reopen then fails ConcurrencyMismatch and B's child reopen aborts with exit 10 despite the parent already being open
